Class JsonPulsarHeaderMapper

java.lang.Object
org.apache.pulsar.spring.support.header.AbstractPulsarHeaderMapper<JsonPulsarHeaderMapper.ToPulsarHeadersContext, JsonPulsarHeaderMapper.ToSpringHeadersContext>
org.apache.pulsar.spring.support.header.JsonPulsarHeaderMapper
All Implemented Interfaces:
PulsarHeaderMapper
public class JsonPulsarHeaderMapper extends AbstractPulsarHeaderMapper<JsonPulsarHeaderMapper.ToPulsarHeadersContext, JsonPulsarHeaderMapper.ToSpringHeadersContext>
A PulsarHeaderMapper implementation that writes headers as JSON.

Allows user to constrain which classes are "trusted" for deserialization as well as configure a list of classes to serialize with a simple "toString".

Author:
Chris Bono

  • Field Details

    • DEFAULT_TRUSTED_PACKAGES

      public static final List<String> DEFAULT_TRUSTED_PACKAGES
      Packages trusted by default for JSON header deserialization. These packages cover the types commonly used in message headers. Add additional packages via JsonPulsarHeaderMapper.JsonPulsarHeaderMapperBuilder.trustedPackages(String...); use "*" to trust all packages (not recommended for untrusted message sources).

    • trusted

      protected boolean trusted(String requestedType)
      Determines whether a type is trusted for JSON deserialization.

      A type is trusted when any of the following is true:

      • It is JsonPulsarHeaderMapper.NonTrustedHeaderType itself (always needed for propagation).
      • It is one of the primitive-array short-forms in TRUSTED_ARRAY_TYPES.
      • The set of trusted packages is empty — which only occurs when the caller has explicitly passed "*" via the builder — meaning all types are trusted.
      • The type's package name exactly matches one of the trusted package entries. Sub-packages are not trusted transitively; add them explicitly if needed.
      Parameters:
      requestedType - fully-qualified class name to evaluate
      Returns:
      true if the type may be deserialized from a message header
